ideas.description: Exploit and add margin. On the E025 incumbent (5x24 + 2x28 + 4x32 px, 2/3/3 net, Muon at batch 1536 with momentum 0.655, Turbo preconditioning plus 2 NS steps, CUDA graphs per resolution, Lookahead and triangle), raise the Muon peak lr by 1.25x, from 0.205 to 0.256, and change nothing else. The SGD groups, momentum, schedule shape and resolution schedule stay fixed. The LR lives in the GPU schedule tensor, so the graphs need no recapture. Rationale: the E024 note says Turbo preconditioning shrank the effective update on the big layers by about 1/3, and the inherited Hiverge lr was tuned for a 3/3/3 CIFAR-10 net without resizing. Run salt 0 (official) and also salt 1, so the comparison is against the pooled E025/E027 estimate of 0.7533 and not E025's single draw of 0.7539.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%, about 7.34 s). 2-salt mean accuracy +0.1 to +0.3 pp over the pooled 0.7533, i.e. about 0.7545-0.7565. If the 2-salt mean is >=0.7553 (+0.2 pp), keep it: that margin pays for the next time cuts. If it is <=0.7513, the lr was already high: run 0.8x (0.164) next. If it falls in between, the result is inconclusive; close the lr axis.

ideas.description: Exploit by removing high-resolution backward work that carries little accuracy. On E025, train the whitening-conv bias only during the 24 px phase (epochs 1-5). In the 28 px and 32 px phases, detach the whitening-layer output (after its activation) before group 1. Autograd then skips the dgrad of the first 128-channel conv and the whitening BN/activation backward at the highest resolutions. In the optimizer, drop the whitening bias from those phases' parameter list, or zero its LR. The 28 and 32 px graphs are captured in build with the detach already in place, and the 24 px graph is unchanged, so no new graph count and no recapture in the timed region. Log per-phase ms/step.
ideas.expected: 28/32 px ms/step falls 2-4%, so total time falls 1-2% (about -0.08 to -0.15 s, to about 7.2-7.27 s). This is work removed, so it should carry over to the PCIe judge (H5.1). Accuracy within ±0.15 pp of the pooled 0.7533, since airbench also freezes the whitening bias after about 3 epochs. Keep it if the 3-seed mean is >=0.753 and time is >=1% lower. If accuracy falls by >=0.25 pp, the whitening bias needs the full-res phase; refute H2.4.4.

ideas.description: Exploit the resolution ladder one rung lower. On E025, run epochs 1-2 at 20 px instead of 24 px, so the schedule becomes 2x20 + 3x24 + 2x28 + 4x32 (11 epochs in total, the same LR schedule over total steps). Use whole augmented images downscaled with bilinear F.interpolate after the 2 px translate crop, as for 24/28 px, and keep the AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) head. Batch 1536 with drop_last. Capture and warm up a 4th CUDA graph (20 px) in build. Rationale: the first epochs learn coarse features and the triangle is still warming up, so resolution matters least there. E020 and E025 both gained from cheaper early pixels.
ideas.expected: A 20 px epoch costs about 0.40-0.44 s versus about 0.54 s at 24 px, so time falls about 0.2-0.28 s (-3 to -4%, to about 7.06-7.14 s). Accuracy falls 0.05-0.3 pp, centred near -0.15 pp (about 0.752 expected). If the 3-seed mean is >=0.753, keep it. If it falls between 0.750 and 0.753, combine it with any free margin gain (the Muon lr idea) or add +0.25 epoch at 32 px; the net should still be about -0.1 s. If it falls below 0.750, the low-res floor is 24 px.

ideas.description: Explore cutting the fixed per-step cost (Muon ~1.5 ms/step after E024, plus Lookahead and launch costs) in the cheap low-res phase. On E025, use batch 3072 in the 24 px phase only (epochs 1-5, 16 steps/epoch with drop_last instead of 32). In that phase, scale the Muon lr by sqrt(2) (0.29) and the SGD-group lr linearly (2x), with momentum unchanged. Keep batch 1536 at 28 and 32 px. Define the LR schedule per step over the new total step count, keeping the same epoch boundaries. Capture the 24 px graph at batch 3072 in build (one graph per resolution, as now).
ideas.expected: About 80 fewer optimizer steps, and the 24 px convs run at a larger, more efficient batch. Low-res phase time falls 8-12%, so total time falls 2-4% (about -0.15 to -0.25 s). Accuracy falls 0.05-0.3 pp: E017 and E022 show that fewer steps cost some accuracy, though less in the under-fit early phase. Keep it if the 3-seed mean is >=0.753 and time is >=2% lower. If accuracy falls by >=0.3 pp, early-phase step count matters; refute H2.3.3.

ideas.description: Measure the exchange rate and build a safe-margin fallback. On E025, add 0.5 epoch at 32 px (5x24 + 2x28 + 4.5x32, LR schedule over total steps) and change nothing else. A 0.5-epoch step is about 2x the measured trajectory noise, so unlike the 0.25-epoch trim of E021 its effect can be read. The result fixes the pp/s line against which E024-style cuts and the 20 px and batch ideas are scored. It also gives the config to fall back on if the official 40-seed mean of E025 looks marginal (pooled 0.7533).
ideas.expected: Time +0.42 s (about 7.76 s). Accuracy +0.35 to +0.6 pp over the pooled 0.7533, i.e. about 0.757-0.759. This gives a slope of 0.8-1.4 pp/s. It will not beat E025 on time, so log it as calibration (discard). If the gain is <0.25 pp, the 32 px tail is saturating: per-step cuts are worth less than assumed, and future margin should come from schedule or lr changes rather than epochs.

ideas.description: Explore the last untested direction of the label-smoothing knob on the current recipe. On E025, raise label smoothing from 0.3 to 0.4 in all phases, and change nothing else. ls is a constant in the loss, so recapture the graphs in build. Rationale: E012 (0.3 to 0.2 lost 0.21 pp) shows that more output regularization helped. With 100 classes and an under-fit, heavily augmented 11-epoch schedule, the optimum may sit above 0.3.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Accuracy -0.15 to +0.25 pp, with a weak prior near +0.1 pp (about 0.7543). Keep it only if the 3-seed mean is >=0.7553 (+0.2 pp over the pooled 0.7533). In that case spend the gain on the 20 px start. A drop of >=0.15 pp closes the ls axis at 0.3.

structured_output.summary:
The queue had no queued ideas left, so I added 6 (4 exploit, 2 explore). The binding constraint is margin: pooling E025 and its salted re-run (E027) puts the incumbent's expected accuracy at about 0.7533, right at the 0.753 bar. Accuracy deltas are judged against that pooled figure, not E025's single draw of 0.7539.

1. **Muon lr 1.25x (H1.7.6), priority 5.** A free accuracy gain is the most valuable result now. The rationale is that Turbo preconditioning shrank the effective update by about a third.
2. **Whitening bias trained only in the 24 px phase, then detached (H2.4.4), priority 4.** This removes work in the 28/32 px phases and needs no extra graph. Expected time -1 to -2% with accuracy unchanged.
3. **20 px for the first 2 epochs (H2.3), priority 3.** Extends the resolution ladder. Expected -3 to -4% time for about -0.15 pp; pair it with any margin gain.
4. **Batch 3072 in the 24 px phase only (H2.3.3), priority 2.** Halves the fixed Muon cost per low-res step. Riskier for accuracy.
5. **+0.5 epoch at 32 px (H1.8.1), priority 2.** Measures the pp/s slope and gives a safe fallback config. It won't beat E025 on time, so it is calibration only.
6. **Label smoothing 0.4 (H1.3.1), priority 2.** The last untested direction of that knob; time-neutral.

No queued ideas needed dropping. I left H1.2.1 alone because alternating flip is already in the recipe, and skipped H1.6.2 and H2.4.3 because their priors are weak. H4.3 (dev seeds) isn't a file change, so it can't be an idea here.
